We also fully characterize the law of the exit point when the process is initially distributed according to its quasistationary distribution. In particular, we work on domains in which the absorbing (Dirichlet) and reflecting (Neumann) parts of the boundary meet tangentially, without forming any non-trivial angle, a configuration that raises genuine regularity difficulties for the solutions of the associated mixed boundary value problem.
item.dc:creator: Louis Carillo (CERMICS UMR 9032), Lo{\"i}s Delande (AGM - UMR 8088), Boris Nectoux (LMBP)

item.title: A direct obstacle proof of a dimension-free weak-type $(1,1)$ bound for the Gaussian Riesz transforms
item.description: arXiv:2610.26478v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a detailed, direct proof of a dimension-free weak-type $(1,1)$ estimate for the first-order Gaussian vector Riesz transform, using the fractional obstacle method of Ouyang, Spector, and Stockdale. For $d\gamma_n=\pi^{-n/2}e^{-|x|^2}\,dx$, let $L=-\tfrac12\Delta+x\cdot\nabla$, $D=2^{-1/2}\nabla$, and $R_\gamma=DL^{-1/2}\Pi_0$, where $\Pi_0$ removes the mean. We prove that $R_\gamma$ has weak-type constant at most $2$ on real-valued inputs, independently of $n$. The main construction is the unique unshifted decomposition $F=g+L^{1/2}u$, for nonnegative $F\in L^2(\gamma_n)$ and $a>\int F\,d\gamma_n$, with $u\geq0$, $\min\{F,a\}\leq g\leq a$, preservation of mass, and $g=a$ on $\{u>0\}$. We retain the details of coercivity, the Lewy--Stampacchia estimate, the upgrade from the form domain to the operator domain, and locality. We also identify the $L^1$ extension with the principal-value transform and obtain the constant $8/\pi$ for complex-valued inputs.
item.dc:creator: Cristian E. Guti\'errez, Juan Manfredi

item.title: Narrow escape problems beyond spherical holes: slits and tubes
item.description: arXiv:2610.26514v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The narrow escape problem consists in characterizing the exit event of a Brownian motion trapped inside a domain with reflecting boundary and small absorbing holes.Using recent advances in the quasi-stationary distribution approach, we first give an explicit set of hypotheses that allows one to derive the asymptotics of the exit time and of the exit hole distribution. We then apply it in dimension three to several hole shapes: spherical holes, thin spheroidal holes shrinking to curves on the boundary (slits), and holes located at the end of thin tubes attached to the domain. We illustrate the accuracy of the results with numerical simulations, and extend them to higher dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Louis Carillo

item.title: Effective intrinsic ergodicity and the transport-entropy inequality: a relation and applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.26588v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Effective intrinsic ergodicity (EIE) quantifies how the pressure defect of an invariant measure controls its distance from an equilibrium state. In this paper, we make explicit the connection between the Einsiedler-Kadyrov-Polo (EKP) inequality, which is central to EIE, and the transport-entropy inequality (TEI). We also extend the finite-state transport-entropy inequality of \cite{CMU19} to topologically mixing countable Markov shifts with the Big Images and Preimages (BIP) property, yielding an EIE estimate in Ornstein's $\bar d$-metric that strengthens \cite{Ruh21}. We also establish a local $\frac{1}{2}$-H\"older bound for the map sending a H\"older potential of finite pressure to its Bowen-Gibbs measure, with respect to the uniform norm on potentials and the $\bar d$-metric on measures. This result extends some aspects of Bhullar's continuity theorem \cite{B25}: it applies to proper subshifts, provides an explicit modulus of continuity with respect to the uniform norm, and does not require strong positive recurrence.
item.dc:creator: Mirmuhsin Maxmud

item.title: Bootstrap percolation on the hypercube
item.description: arXiv:2610.26615v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we obtain the critical probability $p_c(Q_{n},r)$ for bootstrap percolation with the infection threshold $r=f(n)n^a$ on the $n$-dimensional hypercube $Q_{n}$, where $0<a<1$ and $f(n)=n^{o(1)}$. More precisely, we obtain the exact first-order and second-order terms of $p_c(Q_{n},r)$ by extending the main theorem of Balogh, Bollob{\'a}s, and Morris (2009).
item.dc:creator: Fengxing Zhu

item.title: A McLennan formula for equiaccessible steady states
item.description: arXiv:2610.26755v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Near equilibrium, the Boltzmann distribution is corrected by the transient irreversible entropy flux, a result known as the McLennan formula. By expanding around equiaccessible steady states instead, we derive an analogue that can hold arbitrarily far from equilibrium. At zeroth order, steady-state occupation is determined solely by local escape rates, yielding a strong form of the active-matter principle of "low rattling." The first-order correction measures the impact of traffic imbalances on the accessibility of each state, marking the onset of nonlocal determinants of relative occupation.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Calvert

item.title: Improved Mixing Rates of Directed Cycles with Additional Sparse Interconnections
item.description: arXiv:2307.09949v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We analyze the absolute spectral gap of Markov chains on graphs obtained from a cycle of $n$ vertices and perturbed only at approximately $n^{1/\rho}$ random locations with an appropriate, possibly sparse, interconnection structure. Together with a strong asymmetry along the cycle, the gap of the resulting chain can be bounded inversely proportionally by the longest arc length (up to logarithmic factors) with high probability, providing a significant mixing speedup compared to the reversible version.
item.dc:creator: Bal\'azs Gerencs\'er, Julien M. Hendrickx

item.title: Strongly vertex-reinforced jump process on graphs with bounded degree
item.description: arXiv:2401.04366v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study asymptotic behaviours of a non-linear vertex-reinforced jump process defined on an arbitrary infinite graph with bounded degree. We prove that if the reinforcement function $w$ is reciprocally integrable and non-decreasing, then the process visits only a finite number of vertices. In the case where $w$ is regularly varying with index $\alpha>1$, we show that the process eventually gets stuck on a star-shaped subgraph and there is exactly one vertex with unbounded local time.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Collevecchio, Tuan-Minh Nguyen

item.title: A Note on the Stability of Monotone Markov Chains
item.description: arXiv:2401.11568v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This note studies monotone Markov chains, a subclass of Markov chains with extensive applications in operations research and economics. While the properties that ensure the global stability of these chains are well studied, their establishment often relies on the fulfillment of a certain splitting condition. We address the challenges of verifying the splitting condition by introducing simple, applicable conditions that ensure global stability. The simplicity of these conditions is demonstrated through various examples including autoregressive processes, portfolio allocation problems and resource allocation dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Bar Light

item.title: Discrete $N$-particle systems at high temperature through Jack generating functions
item.description: arXiv:2502.13098v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We find necessary and sufficient conditions for the Law of Large Numbers for random discrete $N$-particle systems with the deformation (inverse temperature) parameter $\theta$, as their size $N$ tends to infinity simultaneously with the inverse temperature going to zero. Our conditions are expressed in terms of the Jack generating functions, and our analysis is based on the asymptotics of the action of Cherednik operators obtained via Hecke relations. We apply the general framework to obtain the LLN for a large class of Markov chains of $N$ nonintersecting particles with interaction of log-gas type, and the LLN for the multiplication of Jack polynomials, as the inverse temperature tends to zero. We express the answer in terms of novel one-parameter deformations of cumulants and their description provided by us recovers previous work by Bufetov--Gorin [Geom. Funct. Anal. 25 (2015), no. 3, 763-814] on quantized free cumulants when $\theta=1$, and by Benaych-Georges--Cuenca--Gorin [Comm. Math. Phys. 394 (2022), no. 2, 735-795] after a deformation to continuous space of random matrix eigenvalues. Our methods are robust enough to be applied to the fixed temperature regime, where we recover the LLN of Huang [Adv. Math. 380 (2021), Paper No. 107545, 91].
item.dc:creator: Cesar Cuenca, Maciej Do{\l}\k{e}ga

item.title: Strategic timing of arrivals to a queueing system with scheduled customers
item.description: arXiv:2502.20105v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper examines a single-server queueing system that serves both scheduled and strategic walk-in customers. The service discipline follows a first-come, first-served policy, with scheduled customers granted non-preemptive priority. Each walk-in customer strategically chooses their arrival time to minimise their expected waiting time, taking into account the reservation schedule and the decisions of other walk-in customers. We derive the Nash equilibrium arrival distribution for walk-in customers. We also study the case where early arrivals are allowed and analyse its impact on equilibrium arrival patterns. By analysing various appointment schedules, we assess their effects on equilibrium arrival behaviour, waiting times, and server idle time. Finally, we compare different scheduling policies and evaluate their impact on overall system performance.
item.dc:creator: Wathsala Karunarathne, Camiel Koopmans, Jiesen Wang

item.title: Martingale measure associated with the critical $2d$ stochastic heat flow
item.description: arXiv:2503.20171v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In [CSZ23], the authors proved the convergence of the finite dimensional time distribution of the rescaled random fields derived from the discrete stochastic heat equation of $2d$-directed polymers in random environment in the critical window. The scaling limit is called critical $2d$ stochastic heat flow (SHF). In this paper, we will show that the critical $2d$ SHF is a continuous semimartingale. Moreover, we will consider the martingale problem associated with the critical $2d$ SHF in a similar fashion to the super Brownian motion which is one of the well-known measure valued process. Also, we define the martingale measure associated with the critical $2d$ SHF in the sense of [Wal86, Chapter 2]. The quadratic variation of the martingale measure gives information of the regularity of the critical $2d$ SHF.
item.dc:creator: Makoto Nakashima

item.title: The half-space KPZ line ensemble and its scaling limit
item.description: arXiv:2506.07939v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For each $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}, t\ge 1$, we show that there exists a unique $\mathbb{N}$-indexed line ensemble of random continuous curves $\mathbb{R}_{\le 0} \to \mathbb{R}$ with the following properties: (1) The top curve is distributed as the time-$t$ Cole--Hopf solution to the half-space KPZ equation with narrow wedge initial condition and Neumann boundary condition with parameter $\alpha$. (2) The line ensemble satisfies a one-sided resampling invariance property, involving softly non-intersecting Brownian motions with an attractive potential between pairs at the boundary. We call this object the half-space KPZ line ensemble. For $\alpha=\mu t^{-1/3}$ with $\mu \in \mathbb{R}$ fixed (critical regime) and for $\alpha>0$ fixed (supercritical regime), we show that the half-space KPZ line ensemble near the boundary is tight under 1:2:3 KPZ scaling as $t\to\infty$. Moreover, all subsequential limits approximate a parabola and enjoy a one-sided Brownian Gibbs property, described by non-intersecting Brownian motions with pairwise interaction at the boundary. In the supercritical case, one of the main technical contributions of this paper is the first rigorous demonstration of a structure involving pairwise pinned Brownian motions, previously conjectured in [BCD23]. Away from the boundary, we show that the half-space KPZ line ensemble converges to the (full-space) Airy line ensemble under 1:2:3 KPZ scaling as $t\to\infty$. A key ingredient in our arguments, which may be of independent interest, is a novel identity relating the full- and half-space KPZ equations, which may be valuable in deducing various geometric properties of the latter.
item.dc:creator: Sayan Das, Christian Serio

item.title: On extinction and survival of the Bak-Sneppen model on arbitrary graphs
item.description: arXiv:2506.15500v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the stationary distribution of the discrete Bak--Sneppen model on finite connected graphs of bounded degree, generalizing the model introduced in~\cite{BK}. In the small-$p$ regime, a graphical construction and a comparison with high-density one-dependent oriented site percolation yield a bound of order $p\ln(1/p)$ on the stationary probability that a prescribed vertex has fitness one, uniformly over all such graphs. If the graph can be covered by long chains with bounded overlap, we also obtain an exponential upper tail bound for the stationary density of ones. In the complementary regime, a Lyapunov function argument yields an exponential stationary tail for the number of zeros, uniformly over graphs of a given maximal degree, with explicit parameter bounds.
item.dc:creator: Serguei Popov, Stanislav Volkov

item.title: Persistence probabilities for MA(1) sequences with uniform innovations
item.description: arXiv:2507.04427v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the persistence probabilities of a moving average process of order one with uniform innovations. We identify a number of regions-characterized by the location of the uniform distribution and the coupling parameter of the process-where the persistence probabilities have qualitatively different behaviour. We obtain the generating functions of the persistence probabilities explicitly in all possible regions. In some of the regions, the persistence probabilities can be expressed explicitly in terms of various combinatorial quantities.
item.dc:creator: Frank Aurzada, Kilian Raschel

item.title: Quantitative convergence for displacement monotone Mean Field Games of control
item.description: arXiv:2507.17014v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we establish quantitative convergence results for both open and closed-loop Nash equilibria of N-player stochastic differential games in the setting of Mean Field Games of Controls (MFGC), a class of models where interactions among agents occur through both states and controls. Our analysis covers a general class of non-separable Hamiltonians satisfying a displacement monotonicity condition, along with mild regularity and growth conditions at infinity. A major novelty of our work is the rigorous treatment of a nontrivial fixed-point problem on a space of measures, which arises naturally in the MFGC formulation. Unlike prior works that either restrict to separable Hamiltonians - rendering the fixed-point map trivial - or assume convergence or regularity properties of the fixed point map, we develop a detailed structural analysis of this equation and its N-player analogue. This leads to new regularity results for the fixed-point maps and, in turn, to quantitative convergence of open-loop equilibria. We further derive sharp a priori estimates for the N-player Nash system, enabling us to control the discrepancy between open and closed-loop strategies, and thus to conclude the convergence of closed-loop equilibria. Our framework also accommodates common noise in a natural way.
item.dc:creator: Joe Jackson, Alp\'ar R. M\'esz\'aros

item.title: The Gamma Expansion of the Level Two Large Deviation Rate Functional for Reversible Diffusion Processes
item.dc:creator: Claudio Landim, Jungkyoung Lee, Mauro Mariani

item.title: Strict monotonicity of critical points in independent long-range percolation models
item.description: arXiv:2510.26314v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider independent long-range percolation models on locally finite vertex-transitive graphs. Using coupling ideas we prove strict monotonicity of the critical points with respect to local perturbations in the connection function, thereby improving upon previous results obtained via the classical essential enhancement method of Aizenman and Grimmett in several ways. In particular, our approach allows us to work under minimal assumptions, namely shift-invariance and summability of the connection function, and it applies to both undirected and directed bond percolation models.
item.dc:creator: Stein Andreas Bethuelsen, Christian M\"onch

item.title: A curiously slowly mixing Markov chain
item.description: arXiv:2511.01245v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a Markov chain with very different mixing rates depending on how mixing is measured. The chain is the "Burnside process on the hypercube $C_2^n$." Started at the all-zeros state, it mixes in a bounded number of steps, no matter how large $n$ is, in $\ell^1$ and in $\ell^2$. And started at general $x$, it mixes in at most $\log n$ steps in $\ell^1$. But, in $\ell^2$, it takes $\frac{n}{\log n}$ steps for most starting $x$. The $\ell^2$ mixing results follow from an explicit diagonalization of the Markov chain into binomial-coefficient-valued eigenvectors.
item.dc:creator: Persi Diaconis, Andrew Lin, Arun Ram

item.title: Ergodic Central limit theorem for subgeometric Markov chains
item.description: arXiv:2512.18255v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish verifiable necessary conditions for central limit theorems (CLTs) of ergodic averages of Markov chains on general state spaces. Our criteria are based on discrete-time $\mathbf{L}$-drift conditions that can be verified through estimates for the one-step transition kernel of the original chain. They yield an integral criterion for failure of the CLT for a class of observables that includes unbounded functions and indicators of tail events. The main technical step transfers lower bounds for excursions of the original chain to regenerative excursions of its Nummelin split chain. The same drift conditions yield lower bounds on the tails of return times and modulated excursion functionals, on invariant tails, and on rates of convergence in $f$-variation and $L^p$-Wasserstein distance. These estimates apply without an explicit formula for the invariant distribution. Applications to unadjusted Langevin algorithms show preservation of polynomial target tail indices at every fixed step size. For Euler schemes with additive infinite-variance noise, we establish restrictions on invariant tails and transience under superlinear drifts. Schemes with linear drift, multiplicative noise and logarithmic innovation tails exhibit sharp polynomial convergence exponents and exact CLT thresholds, despite the absence of positive Euclidean moments.
item.dc:creator: Miha Bre\v{s}ar, Aleksandar Mijatovi\'c, Gareth Roberts

item.title: Uniform Limit Theorems for Diffusion Means on Compact Riemannian Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2601.02832v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by Varadhan's theorem, we study Varadhan functions and variances on compact Riemannian manifolds together with their minimizers, the diffusion means introduced in Eltzner et al. (2023). Given independent and identically distributed samples, we prove uniform laws of large numbers and uniform central limit theorems for their empirical versions. Through the small time asymptotics of gradients and Hessians of Varadhan functions, we build a strong connection to the central limit theorem for Fr\'echet means on compact Riemannian manifolds by recovering the ``non-standard'' correction term from Hotz et al. (2024).
item.dc:creator: Yueqi Cao

item.title: Convergence of Half-Space Last Passage Percolation Away from the Boundary to the Directed Landscape
item.description: arXiv:2602.17992v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this note, we prove convergence of the half-space exponential last passage percolation (LPP) model, away from the boundary, to the directed landscape. Our approach couples the half-space and full-space LPP models and constructs two barrier events based on the monotonicity of last passage paths. Combining this coupling with moderate deviation estimates for both models and the known convergence of full-space LPP to the directed landscape, we establish the desired convergence.
item.dc:creator: Xinyi Zhang

item.title: Bulk Directed Landscape Convergence and Phase Transitions in Half-Space Models
item.description: arXiv:2602.23549v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the effects of the boundary in the bulk of two half-space models. For half-space exponential last passage percolation (LPP) and the half-space log-gamma polymer, we establish convergence of their respective rescaled last passage time and free energy to the directed landscape when the observation window is at distance $f(n)n^{2/3}$ from the boundary and the attractive boundary strength is $o(f(n)n^{-1/3})$, where $f(n)\to\infty$ may diverge arbitrarily slowly. We also show that this condition on the boundary strength is sharp at the level of scales: any boundary strength of order $f(n)n^{-1/3}$ changes the limiting behavior for sufficiently large temporal separations. For exponential LPP, we prove a phase transition in the point-to-point last passage time as the boundary attraction varies on the scale \(f(n)n^{-1/3}\). As the attraction increases, the fluctuations transition from a bulk-dominated KPZ regime to a boundary-dominated Gaussian regime, with a critical window governed by the positive part of a shifted Gaussian. The limiting law in the critical window manifests the competition between a Gaussian boundary contribution and a bulk contribution whose magnitude vanishes under the Gaussian scaling.
item.dc:creator: Xinyi Zhang

item.title: "Game, Set, Match": Double Delight Watching a Grand Slam Tennis Match
item.description: arXiv:2603.02360v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Probabilistic properties of tennis scoring systems are examined and compared with best-of-K systems. A model, where each player has his/her own probability of winning his/her service point and which remains invariant for the duration of the match, and where outcomes of points played are independent of each other, is assumed. Probabilities of winning a game tie-breaker, a game, a set tie-breaker, a set, and the match are obtained. Since tennis scoring systems are unique, probability calculations require decomposing big and complicated problems into smaller and simpler constituent problems, solving these sub-problems, then combining to obtain the solution to the big problem. The problems that arise from tennis scoring systems offer excellent pedagogical venues for teaching probability, in particular, the use of the Theorem of Total Probability and the Iterated Rules for Mean, Variance, and Covariance. There are also many interesting questions in tennis, foremost of which is whether a tennis match under this assumption will actually end with probability one; or whether when two players of `equal abilities' play a match, the first server possesses an advantage. These questions are addressed in this work. Tennis scoring systems are technically statistical decision systems to determine the better player. Since such a decision system is based on a finite number of points played, erroneous decisions could arise, such as the inferior player winning the match. We compare different systems in terms of the probability of the better player winning, as well as the duration of the match in terms of the number of points played.
item.dc:creator: Edsel A. Pena, Dip Das, Yuexuan Wu

item.title: Convergence of $k$-point functions in high dimensional percolation
item.description: arXiv:2604.08462v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish first-order asymptotics for the $k$-point connectivity function in critical Bernoulli percolation on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ assuming $d>6$ and Hara's two-point asymptotic. For every $k\ge 3$ and distinct macroscopically separated locations, the probability that the corresponding lattice points lie in the same open cluster, rescaled by $n^{(4-d)(k-1)-2}$, converges as $n \to \infty$ to an explicit sum of integrals indexed by trees. This confirms a conjecture of Aizenman and Newman. We also establish convergence of chemical-distance-decorated $k$-point functions. Conditionally on a set of $k$ point lying in the same cluster, this identifies the joint limiting distribution of all pairwise chemical distances after quadratic rescaling. It is described by binary trees with explicit laws along the edges. The decorated expansion also gives $k$ point asymptotics in the near-critical window. Our proof uses our previous results on convergence to the incipient infinite clusters to decouple macroscopic connections, as well as distributional convergence of the chemical distance.
item.dc:creator: Shirshendu Chatterjee, Pranav Chinmay, Jack Hanson, Philippe Sosoe

item.title: Sofic measures
item.description: arXiv:2604.11212v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Sofic measures, also known as hidden Markov measures, have been extensively studied. In this paper, we survey some equivalent definitions of this notion and improve a bound for deciding whether a sofic measure is~$k$-step Markov. We prove that if an invariant sofic measure with a linear representation of dimension~$n$ is a~$k$-step Markov chain, then~$k$ can be chosen at most equal to~$\binom{n}{2}$ and that this bound is tight for sofic measures over an alphabet of size $3$.
item.dc:creator: Marie-Pierre B\'eal, Vincent Jug\'e, Eugene Gilburg, Jean Mairesse, Dominique Perrin

item.title: Seasonal Statistics of Shannon Rate in a Dynamical Poisson-Voronoi Cellular Network
item.description: arXiv:2605.16560v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work we consider a dynamical cellular communication network in which mobile base stations (BSs) are modeled as a homogeneous Poisson point process on $\mathbb{R}^2$. Each base station moves at a constant speed in a random direction. A typical user connects to the nearest base station and it experiences variable signal and interference powers depending on the distance of all the stations. Along the motion of the stations, the user swaps its serving station, and such an event is called a {\em handover}. We are interested in the performance evaluation of the system under some classical and tropical metrics of interest at different time of events, inducing handovers, maximal proximity of serving station, nearest interferer at closest or farthest distance with respect to the user or at any typical time epoch. The main results of the paper are closed or integral form expressions for the basic metrics of interest, in particular coverage probability and Shannon rate at these epochs. We can make an analogy with ``seasons'' based on the fluctuations of signal and interference power. Strong or mild signal or interference power correspond to different seasons of Shannon rate along the evolution of the system. We also provide a complete comparison study of the metrics at interest at these epochs. We also provide a recipe to lift our results for a 3D wireless communication model for UAVs and HAPS.
item.dc:creator: Sanjoy Kumar Jhawar, Fran\c{c}ois Baccelli

item.title: From smooth to discontinuous kernels: a variance transfer principle for hyperuniform processes
item.description: arXiv:2606.22940v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a transfer principle for the fluctuations of linear statistics of finite particle systems around Lebesgue measure: if for a smooth kernel the variance decays polynomially with some exponent a compared to independent (non-interacting) particles, then the number variance over balls centred at almost every point decays with exponent min(1,a) times a log term if a=1, over a possibly reduced range of scales for non-periodic systems. We apply this principle to eigenvalues of random N*N Girko matrices, leveraging results of Cipolloni et al., and obtain the optimal perimeter-like number variance, on the microscopic and some mesoscopic scales range, after local averaging. We also apply the results to Coulomb gases, by transferring the results of Serfaty: we prove that 2D-Coulomb gases are 2-hyperuniform, i.e. they have surface order number variance, which is optimal, and that 3D Coulomb gases are 1-hyperuniform. In 2D, it allows to prove finite Coulomb energy and Wasserstein distance to Lebesgue measure.
item.dc:creator: Rapha{\"e}l Lachi{\`e}ze-Rey (MATHNET,MAP5 - UMR 8145)

item.title: Relaxation times of non-reversible Markov processes
item.description: arXiv:2607.10801v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a systematic approach to quantify $L^2$-relaxation times for non-reversible Markov processes based on the singular value gap of the generator introduced by Chatterjee. The inverse of the singular value gap is equivalent to the relaxation time of the time-averaged transition semigroup. We show that, moreover, the inverse singular value gap of the two-point motion is equivalent to the relaxation time of the non-averaged transition semigroup, and that it provides a lower bound on the usual spectral gap of the generator. We then introduce a method for deriving lower bounds on singular value gaps for Markov processes with degenerate noise that is based on the concept of a first- and second-order collapse of the generator. It follows ideas from hypocoercivity developed in a previous series of works but is simpler and more broadly applicable. In contrast to previous results, it includes settings with non-vanishing first-order collapse, and thus applies directly to Markov chains (in continuous time), but also to diffusion processes and piecewise-deterministic Markov processes. Our approach yields sharp upper and lower bounds for several classes of examples. First applications include the proof of a conjecture by Diaconis and Miclo on a square-root speed-up for lifted random walks on abelian groups, as well as bounds on relaxation times of switching flows perturbed by noise and of non-reversible diffusion processes.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Eberle, Francis L\"orler

item.title: Invasion dynamics with vanishing fitness for a quasi-critical birth-death process
item.description: arXiv:2609.15269v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the invasion dynamics of populations exhibiting positive density-dependent effects. We start with a single individual and consider a single-type birth and death process. The initial individual growth rate vanishes but it increases with the population density, proportionally to the number of individuals divided by a scaling parameter $K$. Before reaching the macroscopic scale~$K$, the population process is almost critical. We prove that the probability for the population to reach the macroscopic level $K$ decreases as $1/\sqrt{K}$ as $K$ goes to infinity. We also describe the associated trajectories and show that invasion can be split into three time periods. First, the process needs to escape from zero, and conditioning on survival, it grows linearly until the order $\sqrt{K}$. The scaled process is approximated by a diffusion, as for critical branching process, with an additional drift term coming from cooperation, which breaks the branching property. Second, in intermediate scale $\sqrt{K}$, we observe another diffusion, surviving with positive probability, without conditioning. Finally, beyond $\sqrt{K}$ scale, the process can be approximated by a classical macroscopic ODE limit. The proof of the first phase involves change of probability and characterization of uniform integrability of martingales, while the two other phases rely on uniform approximations on polynomial time scales.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Bansaye, Nadia Belmabrouk, Xavier Erny, Simon Girel

item.title: Representations of solutions to Stein equations and their derivatives
item.description: arXiv:2609.17881v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose pointwise representations of the Stein solution to a weighted first-order Stein equation associated with a univariate absolutely continuous distribution. The representation extends to all the derivatives of the solution and with respect to any derivative of the test function. The mechanism behind these representations is an array of kernels that satisfy two key identities, yielding a specific calculus for the Stein framework considered here. The representations record every correction term appearing by differentiation, explaining how choosing the Stein kernel as weight has a special role in Taylor and pairing arguments. The calculus of the kernel extends these representations to any order and exhibits natural and explicit conditions to obtain a one term representation of the $n$-th derivative of the solution with respect to exactly one of the three neighbouring test-function orders of derivatives, \(n-1,n,n+1\). These conditions are simple to ensure by choosing the weight accordingly. The representations yield pointwise envelopes, uniform and weighted Stein factors, and ensure sharpness of the constants. We recover the known sharp results for the Gaussian and the Gamma distribution, improve known factors for the rest of the integrated Pearson family, which is the family under which every correction term cancels. We also study the Subbotin and symmetrized Maxwell families, for which the formulas retain additional pointwise terms. Applications sharpen constants in known distributional approximations and use the higher-order calculus to obtain Edgeworth corrections for the Beta approximation of the P\'olya--Eggenberger urn and the quartic Subbotin approximation in the critical Curie--Weiss model.
item.dc:creator: Ferdinand Rapin, Yvik Swan

item.title: Gaussian fluctuations for the stochastic wave equation with drift
item.description: arXiv:2609.21258v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we study the spatial fluctuations of the solution to the stochastic wave equation with a nonlinear drift and multiplicative Gaussian noise in dimensions one and two. The noise is white in time, and its spatial covariance is either integrable or given by a Riesz kernel; space-time white noise in dimension one is also included. We establish spatial ergodicity, convergence of the rescaled covariance, and prove a quantitative central limit theorem for the spatial fluctuations. We also obtain the corresponding functional central limit theorem. Our approach exploits the compact support of the wave kernel to obtain an estimate for the spatially integrated second Malliavin derivative which is compatible with a bound for the total variation. Further arguments based on the Clark-Ocone formula are used to control the drift contributions.
item.dc:creator: Raluca M. Balan, William D. Stephenson

item.title: Localization Lengths for Two-Dimensional Random Band Matrices: Stretched-Exponential Lower Bounds
item.description: arXiv:2609.24426v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider $N \times N$ random band matrices $H = (H_{xy})$ with centered complex Gaussian entries, indexed by points $x,y$ on the two-dimensional discrete torus $(\mathbb{Z} / \sqrt{N} \mathbb{Z})^2$. The matrix entries $H_{xy}$ vanish whenever the distance between $x$ and $y$ exceeds a constant multiple of the bandwidth parameter $W$. We prove that, for any fixed $\varepsilon>0$, if $W\geq(\log N)^{2+\varepsilon}$, then all bulk eigenvectors are delocalized with high probability. Equivalently, this yields a lower bound of order $\exp(W^{1/2-\varepsilon})$ on the localization length of two-dimensional random band matrices for arbitrarily small constant $\varepsilon>0$, improving the superpolynomial lower bound $W^C$ for every fixed constant $C>0$ established in arXiv:2503.07606. A key ingredient of our proof is a new strategy that closes the resolvent flow analysis using only loop observables of order at most two, without relying on the higher-order loop hierarchy.
item.dc:creator: Xujie Lai, Fan Yang

item.title: Spectra of Random Polynomial Matrices: the Petaloid Law
item.description: arXiv:2609.40232v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the distribution of the zeros of $\det P_N(z)$ where $P_N(z)$ is a random monic polynomial matrix, i.e., $P_N(z)=z^dI-\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}A_{j,N}z^j$ for possibly coupled random matrices $A_{j,N}$, scaled to have entrywise variance $O(1/N)$. We provide general conditions under which this distribution almost-surely weakly converges as $N\to\infty$ to a deterministic measure, depending on just the variance and covariance of the entries of the $A_j$. This generalizes the circular, elliptic, and semicircle laws, which concern the special case of this question where $d=1$. Unlike those classical laws, these measures can combine nonuniform two-dimensional densities with singular components supported on curves, producing a variety of petal-shaped regions, inspiring our name ``the petaloid law''. We give explicit formulas for the limiting densities and supports. Under a Gaussianity assumption, we also show that there are almost surely no eigenvalues outside small neighborhoods of the limiting support.
item.dc:creator: Rikhav Shah, Edward Zeng

item.title: Limit law for Brownian cover time of the two dimensional torus
item.description: arXiv:2610.03555v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}_\varepsilon$ denote the time it takes a Brownian motion to come within distance $\varepsilon$ of every point in the two dimensional torus $\mathbb{T}^2$ of unit area. We prove that for an explicit non-random centering $m_\varepsilon$, the variables $\{\sqrt{\mathcal{C}_{\varepsilon}} - m_\varepsilon \}$ converge in distribution as $\varepsilon \to 0$, to a randomly shifted Gumbel law.
item.dc:creator: Amir Dembo, Jay Rosen, Ofer Zeitouni

item.title: Seed thresholds and degree variance in heterogeneous bootstrap percolation with growing degrees
item.description: arXiv:2610.04420v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study bootstrap percolation with independent vertex thresholds taking values one and two, with threshold-one probability $(1-c/d)/d$ for fixed $c>0$. The seed set is chosen uniformly among sets of a prescribed deterministic size, independently of the graph and thresholds. We prove threshold statements at fixed relative margins. For uniform simple graphs with prescribed nonnegative integer degrees of even sum and exact mean $d$, assume $\max_i|d_i-d|\le C\sqrt d$ and $c+1-v_n\ge\kappa>0$, where $v_n=\operatorname{Var}(D)/d$ and $C,\kappa$ are fixed. When $d\to\infty$ and $d=o(n^{1/7})$, the leading seed scale is $n(c+1-v_n)^2/(2d^4)$, without requiring a limit of $v_n$. At fixed relative margins below and above this scale, the final active set has size $O(n/d^3)$ and $n-o(n)$, respectively, with high probability. For regular graphs, the supercritical conclusion strengthens to full activation. For $G(n,d/n)$, the same $O(n/d^3)$ and $n-o(n)$ conclusions hold when $d\to\infty$ and $d^5/n\to0$, with seed scale $nc^2/(2d^4)$. Thus regular and independent-edge graphs have different coefficients at the same asymptotic mean degree. Local exploration estimates yield explicit inactive remainders and survive conditioning on simplicity in the prescribed model. We also quantify the precision obstruction to static inclusion transfer and compute deterministic response-barrier corrections, without identifying a shrinking random critical window.
item.dc:creator: Aleksandr Rodionov

item.title: Uniform Bessel bounds for magnetization crossings in finite Ising chains
item.description: arXiv:2610.06935v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider a finite Ising chain in zero field and ask when the all-up configuration is as likely as zero magnetization (magnetization one for an odd number of spins). For both free and periodic ends, the crossing coupling of a long chain is half the logarithm of its length minus half the logarithm of that logarithm, up to a term that vanishes as the length grows. We compute further terms with explicit constants and, for free ends, bound the crossing at every length. The second term is missing from an earlier approximation and explains why an earlier numerical fit gives a slope below one half. To locate the crossing, we compare the known magnetization law with its Bessel approximation. The Bessel approximation is above the exact weight, and we bound its relative error for every length, coupling and magnetization. At the crossing this bound tends to zero. The central bin still has about as many domain walls as the logarithm of the length on average, so the crossing has a coupling width of order the inverse logarithm. In a fixed positive dimensionless field the last crossing comes from near the edge of the row, at a coupling of about a quarter of the logarithm of the length. For long chains it is the one-spin crossing when the field exceeds half the logarithm of two. Below that value another bin crosses later.
item.dc:creator: Arjun Pemmasani

item.title: Functional limit theorems for weighted occupation times of supercritical superprocesses
item.description: arXiv:2610.12503v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Suppose $X=(X_t)_{t\ge0}$ is a supercritical superprocess with a non-local branching mechanism on a Lusin space $E$, whose mean semigroup admits a positive leading eigenvalue $\lambda_1$ with a bounded positive eigenfunction $\varphi$ and a finite eigenmeasure $\widetilde{\varphi}$. Let $Y_t:=\int_0^t X_s\mathrm{d}s$ be its occupation measure. We first prove a law of large numbers, that is, for every bounded measurable function $f$, $e^{-\lambda_1 t}\langle f,Y_t\rangle$ converges in $L^2$ to $\lambda_1^{-1}\langle f,\widetilde{\varphi}\rangle W^\varphi_\infty$, where $W^\varphi_\infty$ is the limit of the martingale $W^\varphi_t:=e^{-\lambda_1 t}\langle\varphi,X_t\rangle$. We then establish functional central limit theorems for the fluctuations of $\langle f,Y_t\rangle$ around this random centering. We show that the normalisation and the limit are determined by the spectral decay rate of $f$ compared with the critical value $\lambda_1/2$, and there are three possible regimes: after suitable normalisation, the fluctuation process converges in distribution in $\mathcal{C}[0,+\infty)$ either to a mixed Gaussian process $\sqrt{W^{\varphi}_{\infty}}G(f)$, or to a constant Gaussian process with random variance depending on $W^{\varphi}_{\infty}$, or to a non-Gaussian limit given by the limit of a martingale associated with the spectral projection of $f$. These results are the occupation-time counterparts of the fluctuation theorems for instantaneous linear functionals of supercritical non-local branching superprocesses.
item.dc:creator: Ting Yang

item.title: Cutoff profiles and boundary effects in the Togashi-Kaneko model of autocatalytic reactions with weak mutations
item.description: arXiv:2610.17775v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine explicit bulk and worst-case total variation cutoff profiles for the configuration law of a two-species Togashi--Kaneko model with a fixed population of $n$ particles and weak mutations. Boundary initial conditions introduce an additional logarithmic growth phase and change both the leading mixing-time coefficient and the limiting cutoff profile. Let $\kappa_1,\kappa_2>0$ be the autocatalytic rate constants and put $\lambda_*=\kappa_1\kappa_2/(\kappa_1+\kappa_2)$. For deterministic initial configurations whose density converges to $m\in(0,1)$, the total variation distance to equilibrium at time $t_n(s)=\frac{\log n}{2\lambda_*}+\frac{s}{\lambda_*}$ converges to $\mathcal G(r(m)e^{-s})$ for every fixed $s\in\mathbb R$, where $\mathcal G(r)=\mathrm{d}_{\mathsf{TV}}(\mathcal N(r,1),\mathcal N(0,1))$, $r(m)>0$ is explicit, and $\mathcal N(a,b^2)$ denotes the Gaussian distribution with mean $a$ and variance $b^2$. For the worst-case distance $\mathscr D_n(t)$ over all initial configurations, we prove $\mathscr D_n(T_n+s/\lambda_*)\to\mathcal P(s)$, where $T_n=\left(\frac{1}{\min\{\kappa_1,\kappa_2\}}+\frac{1}{2\lambda_*}\right)\log n$.The profile $\mathcal P$ is the total variation distance between the equilibrium Gaussian and a Gaussian mixture whose random displacement is determined by a gamma-distributed amplitude arising from early growth at the boundary. Unlike the bulk profile, $\mathcal P$ depends on the mutation parameters. Both cutoffs have windows of constant order, and we identify the asymptotically worst boundary configurations.
item.dc:creator: Yangrui Xiang, Wasiur R. KhudaBukhsh

item.title: Drift and joint minimal displacement for groups acting on hyperbolic spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.19787v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We obtain a uniform lower bound for the drift of random walks on hyperbolic spaces in terms of joint minimal displacement. Our main theorem applies to weakly acylindrical actions on Gromov-hyperbolic spaces and is quantitative in all relevant constants. For discrete isometry groups of Hadamard manifolds with pinched negative curvature, the required assumptions are automatically satisfied by the Margulis lemma. This yields uniform gaps at zero in drift spectra for pinched negatively curved Hadamard manifolds, hyperbolic groups, and mapping class groups acting on curve graphs.
item.dc:creator: Koji Fujiwara, Ryokichi Tanaka

item.title: Dipole Formation in the Two-Component Plasma
item.description: arXiv:2410.01025v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the two-dimensional two-component plasma, or Coulomb gas, consisting of $N$ positive and $N$ negative charges with logarithmic interaction. We introduce a suitable regularization of the interaction by smearing the charges over a small length scale $\lambda$, which allows us to give meaning to the system in the continuum at any temperature. We provide an expansion of the free energy for each inverse temperature $\beta\ge2$, as $N \to \infty$ and $\lambda \to 0$. Doing so allows us to show that, for $\beta \geq 2$, the charges (for the most part) pair into neutral dipoles of very small size as $\lambda \to 0$. This complements the prior work of Lebl\'e, Zeitouni, and the second author, which proved that this does not happen for $\beta < 2$, thereby implying a transition at $\beta = 2$ from free charges to dipole pairs. Moreover, we obtain an estimate on the size of linear statistics. The description in terms of dipoles is made via a decomposition into nearest-neighbor graphs of the point configurations, \`a la Gunson-Panta. This is combined with new energy estimates obtained via an electric reformulation of the interaction energy and a ball-growth method, which are expressed in terms of the nearest-neighbor graph distances only. In this way, the model is compared to a reduced nearest-neighbor interaction model, by showing the relative smallness of the dipole-dipole interactions.
item.dc:creator: Jeanne Boursier, Sylvia Serfaty

item.title: A Geometric Framework for Stochastic Iterations
item.description: arXiv:2504.02761v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper concerns models and convergence principles for dealing with stochasticity in a wide range of algorithms arising in nonlinear analysis and optimization in Hilbert spaces. It proposes a flexible geometric framework within which existing solution methods can be recast and improved, and new ones can be designed. Almost sure weak, strong, and linear convergence results are established in particular for stochastic fixed point iterations, the stochastic gradient descent method, and stochastic extrapolated parallel algorithms for feasibility problems. In these areas, the proposed algorithms exceed the features and convergence guarantees of the state of the art. Numerical applications to signal and image recovery are provided.
item.dc:creator: Patrick L. Combettes, Javier I. Madariaga

item.title: Asymptotics of Constrained Quantization for Compactly Supported Measures
item.description:
arXiv:2505.10801v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study constrained quantization of a compactly supported probability $P$ on $\mathbb{R}^D$ by codebooks in a nonempty closed set $S$. For $0<r\le\infty$, the constrained error $e_{n,r}$ is attained and satisfies $e_{n,r}\downarrow L_r=\|\operatorname{dist}(\cdot,S)\|_{L^r(P)}$. Set $\Delta_{n,r}=e_{n,r}^r-L_r^r$ for finite $r$. A Borel nearest-point selector $T$ induces $\mu=T_*P$. Writing $q_{n,s}$ for the classical $L^s$ quantization error, we obtain $e_{n,r}-L_r\le2q_{n,r}(\mu)$ and $\Delta_{n,r}\le C_rq_{n,1}(\mu)$ for $1\le r<\infty$, with $C_r$ independent of $n$, and $\Delta_{n,r}\le2^rq_{n,r}(\mu)^r$ for $0<r<1$. Also, $e_{n,\infty}-L_\infty\le2c_n(E)$, where $E$ is the nearest-point image of $\operatorname{supp}P$ and $c_n(E)$ is its covering radius. For $1\le r<\infty$, a weighted power-growth condition with exponent $ eta>0$ on a fixed source set $F$ bounds $\Delta_{n,r}$ below by the classical $ eta$-power quantization cost of $
u_F=T_*(wP|_F)$. If $d
u_F=\widehat w\,d\eta$ for a compactly supported reference probability $\eta$ and $\widehat w\in A_p(\eta)$, $1<p<\infty$, then $\Delta_{n,r}\ge
u_F(\mathbb{R}^D)[\widehat w]_{A_p(\eta)}^{-1}q_{n, eta/p}(\eta)^ eta$. These comparisons yield bounds for the quantization dimensions defined by $e_{n,r}-L_r$ and $\Delta_{n,r}^{1/r}$, with distinct behavior at positive and zero baselines. Convex and uniformly prox-regular constraints supply the growth weights through their projection inequalities. Circle and lifted Cantor distributions give matching quadratic-excess rates, while rectifiable weighted projections give lower Zador estimates.
item.dc:creator: Chenxing Qian

item.title: Cycle lengths in the percolated hypercube
item.description: arXiv:2506.16858v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $Q^d_p$ be the random subgraph of the $d$-dimensional binary hypercube obtained after edge-percolation with probability $p$. It was shown recently by the authors that, for every $\varepsilon > 0$, there is some $c = c(\varepsilon)>0$ such that, if $pd\ge c$, then typically $Q^d_p$ contains a cycle of length at least $(1-\varepsilon)2^d$. We strengthen this result to show that, under the same assumptions, typically $Q^d_p$ contains cycles of all even lengths between $4$ and $(1-\varepsilon)2^d$.
item.dc:creator: Michael Anastos, Sahar Diskin, Joshua Erde, Mihyun Kang, Michael Krivelevich, Lyuben Lichev

item.title: Branched Signature Model
item.description: arXiv:2511.00018v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we introduce the branched signature model, motivated by the branched rough path framework of [Gubinelli, Journal of Differential Equations, 248(4), 2010], which generalizes the classical geometric rough path. We establish a universal approximation theorem for the branched signature model and demonstrate that iterative compositions of lower-level signature maps can approximate higher-level signatures. Furthermore, building on the existence of the extension map proposed in [Hairer-Kelly. Annales de l'Institue Henri Poincar\'e, Probabilit\'es et Statistiques 51, no. 1 (2015)], we show how to explicitly construct the extension of the original paths into higher-dimensional spaces via a map $\Psi$, so that the branched signature can be realized as the classical geometric signature of the extended path. This framework not only provides an efficient computational scheme for branched signatures but also opens new avenues for data-driven modeling and applications. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework through two representative applications: rough volatility calibration and optimal execution.
item.dc:creator: Munawar Ali, Qi Feng

item.title: On the utility problem in a market where price impact is transient
item.description: arXiv:2511.12093v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider a discrete-time model of a financial market where a risky asset is bought and sold with transactions having a transient price impact. It is shown that the corresponding utility maximization problem admits a solution. We manage to remove some unnatural restrictions on the market depth and resilience processes that were present in earlier work. A non-standard feature of the problem is that the set of attainable portfolio values may fail the convexity property.
item.dc:creator: L\'or\'ant Nagy, Mikl\'os R\'asonyi

item.title: Schur--Weyl duality for diagonalizing a Markov chain on the hypercube
item.description: arXiv:2512.23285v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show how the tools of modern algebraic combinatorics -- representation theory, Murphy elements, and particularly Schur--Weyl duality -- can be used to give an explicit orthonormal basis of eigenfunctions for a "curiously slowly mixing Markov chain" on the space of binary $n$-tuples. The basis is used to give sharp rates of convergence to stationarity.
item.dc:creator: Persi Diaconis, Andrew Lin, Arun Ram

item.title: Coherent risk from finite models
item.description: arXiv:2602.00784v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Coherent estimators at different sample sizes need not describe the same population risk. We prove that dyadic estimators do so exactly when duplicating every scenario leaves the estimate unchanged, and recover the population dual set from the finite models. The risk of a Bernoulli loss determines the exact Wasserstein, Kolmogorov and total-variation moduli on a common bounded support. It also characterises uniform estimability, with an impossibility bound for arbitrary randomised estimators. An intrinsic floor on tail levels gives an explicit optimal Lipschitz constant and a uniform approximation defect; every deterministic vanishing floor preserves pointwise strong consistency. A nonstandard construction supplies compatible estimators at all finite sample sizes, explicit block-sum weights, and a formula for the worst-case mass created by infinitesimal tail levels. Finally, we derive uniform regret bounds for data-driven risk-averse optimisation and specialise them to stop-loss retention. Exact binomial calculations compare regularised and original estimators against the same population target.
item.dc:creator: Tomasz Kania

item.title: The record statistic and forward stability of Schubert products
item.description: arXiv:2604.02964v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We initiate a probabilistic study of forward stability for products of Schubert polynomials through the record statistic (left-to-right maxima) of permutations. Building on the explicit record formula for forward stability obtained by Hardt and Wallach, we study random pairs of permutations drawn from three natural families: uniform permutations, Grassmannian permutations, and Boolean permutations. For each family, we determine record probabilities and use them to analyze the asymptotic behavior of forward stability. For uniform and Grassmannian permutations, we obtain asymptotics for the mean together with limiting distribution results. For Boolean permutations, we prove linear-order growth of the mean, and our analysis also produces an explicit time-inhomogeneous Markov chain that yields an exact linear-time uniform sampler. Beyond these cases, we prove that the record-set statistic is equidistributed on the avoidance classes of $132$ and $231$, and consequently the corresponding forward stability distributions coincide. We conclude with conjectures for numerous further permutation classes and a conjectural recursive criterion for when two avoidance classes have the same record-set distribution.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Hardt, Reuven Hodges, Hanzhang Yin

item.title: Second-order geometry of optimal transport: cost identifiability and stability
item.description: arXiv:2604.22670v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the optimal transport value as a functional of the ground cost. Although this functional is an infimum of linear functionals and is therefore polyhedral for finitely supported marginals, it develops genuine second-order geometry in the smooth continuous setting. Under twist, nondegeneracy, and regularity assumptions, we prove twice differentiability with respect to the cost in H\"older spaces, derive a variational formula for the Hessian, and characterize its null space. The resulting curvature is strict transverse to the cost perturbations that preserve the observed optimal plan. This structure yields identifiability and quantitative stability for inverse optimal transport. For bilinear costs $c_A(x,y)=-x^\top Ay$, a full spanning condition on the Hessians of the Kantorovich potential implies that every nonzero matrix compatible with a single optimal coupling is a positive multiple of the true matrix. We show that this condition can be attained by arbitrarily small compactly supported smooth perturbations of the transport potential that preserve the target marginal's support and density class. For $d\ge2$, uniquely optimal discrete plans and same-base elliptical models, including Gaussians, retain nontrivial degeneracies. Finally, we quantify the regularization bias and sampling error of entropic inverse optimal transport as the regularization parameter vanishes. Thus the second-order geometry of the forward transport problem provides a means towards identifiability, stability, and statistical cost recovery.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Peyr\'e, Clarice Poon, Oscar Tron

item.title: SPLIT: SymPathy for Large jobs Improves Tail latency
item.description: arXiv:2605.13749v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the asymptotic response time tail in the M/G/n multi-server queue with heavy-tailed (regularly varying) job sizes, a setting representative of modern computing workloads. For single-server systems, tail optimization is well understood: under heavy-tailed job sizes, policies such as SRPT that strictly prioritize short jobs are strongly tail optimal, and giving any priority to large jobs is harmful. For multi-server systems, the question has been almost entirely open. This paper gives the first strongly tail-optimal scheduling policies for the M/G/n queue with heavy-tailed job sizes. Our central finding is that the multi-server case is intrinsically different from the single-server case: giving a small amount of ``sympathy'' to large jobs is essential for strong tail optimality. We establish strong (or arbitrarily close to strong) tail optimality across the full stability region, both with and without knowledge of job sizes.
item.dc:creator: Zhouzi Li, Mor Harchol-Balter, Alan Scheller-Wolf

item.title: All-out Attack: Optimal Block Withholding Under Pay-Per-Share Scheme
item.description: arXiv:2607.01209v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Classical Block Withholding (BWH) attacks have been extensively studied in block-dependent reward schemes, where pool members are compensated upon a block discovery within the pool. However, most contemporary mining pools operate under share-based schemes, wherein participants are paid immediately upon submission of valid shares. In this paper, we analyze BWH under Pay-Per-Share (PPS) for Nakamoto-style blockchains and prove that these mechanisms are not incentive compatible, contrary to conclusions drawn under fixed difficulty in prior literature. Under PPS, the optimal strategy for a BWH attacker is the All-out Attack (AoA): the adversary allocates its entire hashpower toward the victim pool, submitting only partial Proof-of-Work shares (pPoW) while withholding all valid blocks, i.e., full Proof-of-Work (fPoW). Prior to the first difficulty adjustment, the adversary incurs negligible loss from withheld fPoWs. After the adjustment reduces block difficulty, the adversary either generates more pPoWs per unit time when the pPoW difficulty is reduced accordingly or, if the pPoW difficulty is held fixed, earns a higher reward per share. In both cases, it achieves a post-adjustment reward rate of $\frac{\alpha}{1-\alpha}$ per target epoch, compared with the honest baseline rate of $\alpha$. Remarkably, this gain matches the theoretical upper bound achieved by optimal selfish mining in Nakamoto consensus under perfect network influence. The results further indicate that BWH is substantially more profitable under PPS than under mainstream block-dependent payout schemes, even when compared with advanced BWH variants. Honest miners benefit at the same rate as the adversary per unit hashpower, while the victim pool operator bears all losses, paying out-of-pocket for pPoW submissions without receiving fPoW compensation in return.
item.dc:creator: Mustafa Doger, Sennur Ulukus

item.title: Online Discrepancy for Sub-Exponential Product Distributions via Regularization
item.description: arXiv:2608.10040v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study online discrepancy minimization for independent random vectors in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with independent coordinates. Our deterministic algorithms require no knowledge of the horizon, and their guarantees hold at every prescribed deterministic terminal time $T$. For unit-variance sub-exponential coordinates with $\psi_1$-norms at most $\sigma$, we obtain terminal discrepancy $O(\sigma^4\sqrt n)$ with failure probability $\exp(-\Omega(\sigma^3\sqrt n))$. Independently masking centered unit-variance marks from the same class with retention probability $k/n$ gives $O(\sigma^4\sqrt k)$ discrepancy with failure probability $\exp(-\Omega(\sigma^3\sqrt k))$ when $k\gtrsim\log^2(2n)$. The fourth-power dependence on $\sigma$ is necessary for these sub-exponential classes at the stated confidence levels. For standard Gaussian marks, we obtain $O(\sqrt k+\sqrt{\log(2n)})$ discrepancy with failure probability $\exp(-\Omega(\sqrt k+\sqrt{\log(2n)}))$. Both terms are necessary up to absolute constants for $T\ge n$. In particular, $k\gtrsim\log n$ is the optimal sparsity threshold for $O(\sqrt k)$ discrepancy. For centered unit-variance sub-Gaussian marks with any fixed $\psi_2$-norm bound $\sigma$, logarithmic sparsity suffices for $O(\sigma\sqrt{k\log(e+\sigma)})$ discrepancy with probability tending to one as $n\to\infty$. For a dimension-dependent family of unit-variance laws with rare activations, matching bounds determine the fixed-confidence online discrepancy order $\Theta(\sqrt n\log\log n)$ at sufficiently long prescribed horizons. Our dense result generalizes the Rademacher-input theorem of Bansal and Spencer (2020) and establishes the horizon-independent $O(\sqrt n)$ Gaussian terminal discrepancy scale anticipated by Gamarnik et al. (2022). The proofs combine regularization, global Fenchel estimates, coupled Lyapunov functions, and terminal moment recursions.

item.title: Optimal Loss Allocation and Reflected Free Boundaries in Systemic Risk
item.description: arXiv:2608.18113v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study a singular mean-field control problem in which a central planner allocates losses generated by bank defaults to maximize terminal system health. Every generated loss must be borne by the surviving banks, without external capital. We prove that a cutoff, or "taxing-the-richest" rule is optimal for every non-decreasing concave terminal payoff, including the survival indicator. We construct the continuous-time optimizer by solving a time-discretized problem and passing to the limit, and establish its uniqueness in law for every non-constant payoff. The optimal flow is characterized by a novel reflected free-boundary problem. We establish well-posedness in a probabilistic solution class and prove positive-time smoothness of both the free boundary and the density of surviving banks. The main difficulty is the dependence of the limiting feedback on a moving support endpoint, which is unstable under Wasserstein convergence. We address this through stochastic-order comparisons, compactness estimates for the cutoff boundaries, and an augmented call-function formulation.
item.dc:creator: Yucheng Guo, Qinxin Yan

item.title: Multidimensional fractional material derivative: measure-valued solutions and probabilistic properties
item.description: arXiv:2609.20060v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We analyze a nonlocal operator in space and time, called the multidimensional fractional material derivative. We derive its pointwise representation, which allows us to study its other properties. We define an inverse operator, called fractional material integral, and derive its pointwise representation. Furthermore, we analyze a class of linear partial differential equations, which corresponds to deterministic descriptions of the scaling limits of multidimensional L\'evy walks, in which transport is driven by a multidimensional fractional material derivative with a speed vector integrated with respect to a suitable probability measure and a distributional source term. Using Fourier-Laplace transform techniques and a direct convolution-kernel construction, we prove the existence and uniqueness of exponentially integrable measure solutions for measure data. Moreover, we identify a necessary and sufficient condition on the source term for conservation of unit mass and provide separate sufficient conditions for non-negativity and weak convergence to $\delta_0$. We also prove weak continuity and self-similarity of the kernel and continuous dependence on the directional distribution.

item.title: Optimal Feature-Based Newsvendor Policies under Censored Demand
item.description: arXiv:2610.17465v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate a newsvendor problem where a decision-maker observes a z-dimensional vector of covariates, and wants to learn how much stock to order given a sample of size n of censored demand data to minimize costs. Demand is censored when insufficient stock is available to meet it, and past stocking quantities are known. We propose a new model-agnostic loss function approach to estimate optimal order quantities using observational data, and characterize the optimal newsvendor policy as the policy that minimizes our proposed loss function. Our method requires only a single estimation step, can be scaled to datasets with hundreds of thousands of data points, and does not suffer from the same instabilities as inverse censoring probability weighting methods. We describe how this loss function can be implemented in linear empirical risk minimization, kernel weights optimization and deep neural network algorithms, and provide excess risk generalization bounds for their out-of-sample performance. Moreover, we show through numerical experiments that our method quickly converges to the optimal policy on synthetic data, and leads to improved performance on real world retail data.
item.dc:creator: Joost van der Haar, Ilias Willems, Joachim Arts, Ingrid Van Keilegom

item.title: Quantitative Convergence of Markov Equilibria for Time-Inconsistent Controlled Diffusions
item.description: arXiv:2610.18376v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Time-inconsistent stochastic control admits a natural game-theoretic interpretation in which successive decision dates are represented by different selves. In the Markovian framework of Bj\"ork-Khapko-Murgoci, the corresponding continuous-time equilibrium HJB system can be motivated by discrete subgame-perfect games, but the general discrete-to-continuous passage is not automatic. We establish a quantitative convergence theorem for a smooth uniformly elliptic class with strongly concave Hamiltonians and interior equilibrium controls, allowing control in both drift and diffusion. Using the exact sample-and-hold transition law on each time step, we construct, near a given verified continuous-time BKM weak equilibrium, a unique regular discrete Markov subgame-perfect equilibrium and prove first-order convergence of continuation objects in $C^{2+\beta}$ H\"older norms with mixed regularity and of policies and values uniformly. The key stability mechanism is structural: the discrete first-order condition makes the frozen differential feedback correction nilpotent. A two-norm dyadic Schauder argument, local Gaussian comparison, and spatial localization turn this cancellation into mesh-uniform block stability despite the second-order coupling caused by controlled volatility.
